title: People v. Cabalquinto
summary: The Supreme Court established the rule that in cases involving violence against women and children, the identity of the victim and her immediate family shall be withheld and fictitious initials used. This was to protect the dignity and privacy of victims.
doctrine: In cases involving violence against women and children, the real name of the victim-survivor shall be withheld. Fictitious initials shall be used to represent the victim to protect her dignity and privacy. This rule applies to all stages of the proceedings and to all court issuances.
fullText:
PER CURIAM:

The Court takes this opportunity to address the need to protect the identity of victims of violence, particularly women and children.

Republic Act No. 7610, the Special Protection of Children Against Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act, and RA 9262, the Anti-Violence Against Women and Their Children Act, provide for the confidentiality of proceedings involving child victims.

The Court resolves that in cases involving violence against women and their children, the real name of the victim and her personal circumstances which tend to establish her identity shall be withheld. Fictitious initials shall be used to represent the victim.
